rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS000753 is best supported because it provides the clearest PRS-comparable discriminative evidence via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) alongside a straightforward AAA endpoint (prevalent AAA) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), whereas several newer genome-wide scores mainly report full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only AUROC and with unknown/less-comparable covariate context. Runners-up are ranked by remaining support: PGS003973 and PGS003972 come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis publication family with large multi-cohort development (supportive study archetype) but rely on full-model discrimination metrics (C-index/AUROC) and have limited PRS-only evidence plus unknown/basic covariates; PGS001784 (Global Biobank framework) reports a PRS-comparable R2 (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out 0.014661) but is explicitly a framework-style score and its high full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven; PGS002054 (UKB portability framework) has only a modest partial-r (0.0144) and framework-study penalty. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because across the pool there is no consistently reported PRS-only AUROC, and several candidates’ headline discrimination metrics are full-model and thus not directly comparable for PRS ranking. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported alignment to alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder. PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder", uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), is developed from multi-cohort sources (MVP, UKB), and reports a reasonably strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS002738 has unknown covariates, reducing comparability and keeping confidence below high. Runners-up: PGS000201 and PGS000202 are closely aligned (phenotyping_reported is DSM-5 AUD criteria count) and have explicit incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456, respectively) with known covariates, but they are labeled as "Problematic alcohol use" / "alcohol dependence measurement" and appear UKB-only development; among them PGS000201 ranks above PGS000202 due to higher ΔR² and larger validation n. PGS002739 is also directly aligned (trait_efo="alcohol dependence", AUD phenotype) and reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 in an AFR evaluation sample, but its evaluation ancestry differs (AFR-only) and it is a gene-based sparse score (858 variants), making it less broadly supported for a generic (unspecified-ancestry) target than the EUR-evaluated PGS002738.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis; trait_reported/phenotyping are near-synonymous). PGS004913 is best supported because it is explicitly disease-focused on alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, uses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and reports PRS-comparable variance explained (R²=0.029) plus a sizable stratification effect (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4). The main limitation is that the reported R² is modest and not clearly labeled as PGS-only vs full-model, and overall evidence is heterogeneous across candidates (different metrics and study designs), preventing a high-confidence pick. Runner-up PGS001777 is also disease-focused and reports strong risk stratification (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% 6.18) but is based on only 3 variants, has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390), lowering robustness. PGS000704 is deprioritized despite large training/validation and a higher reported full-model C-index (0.711) because it appears to be a pan-biomarker UKB framework-style model and only reports full-model discrimination (not PGS-only), making its metric less comparable for PRS ranking.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo and closely aligned phenotyping_reported (Angina / I20 ICD10 / PheCode 411.3), so a direct-match exists. The strongest visible PRS-quality evidence comes from the HGG Adv MVP PheCode 411.3 set (PGS005047–PGS005059), which reports per-SD effect sizes with C-index values; within this coherent family, PGS005052 has the strongest reported OR per SD (1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57) with a high C-index (0.7662), making it the best-supported choice on comparable PRS evidence. Runners-up are the closest siblings with similarly strong ORs and C-index: PGS005048 (OR 1.487; C-index 0.7669), PGS005057 (OR 1.479; C-index 0.7664), PGS005051 (OR 1.455; C-index 0.7655), and PGS005050 (OR 1.445; C-index 0.7651). Confidence is only Moderate because many candidates are near-indistinguishable within the MVP family (very small metric differences), and several other direct-match models either lack PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527) or come from pan-trait UKB sparse framework scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) where full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven and framework origin is a known limitation; additionally, some candidates report only full-model metrics or have unknown covariates, limiting clean cross-model comparability.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to ankylosing spondylitis), so a direct-match exists. PGS001267 is preferred because it reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus full-model AUROC with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large European validation (n=67,425), making its performance evidence more directly interpretable than candidates that only report full-model AUROC (PGS003420–PGS003424) or only partial correlation without AUROC/R² (PGS001876, PGS002089). Main limitation: PGS001267 (and PGS001268) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; additionally, several alternatives are hard to compare due to missing PRS-only metrics and differing ancestry contexts (e.g., EAS-only Taiwanese models with unknown covariates). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001268 is a near-clone with slightly higher reported metrics but uses a time-to-event phenotype (a mild endpoint penalty); PGS002089 and PGS001876 have stronger methodological/variant-count signals within the UKB portability family but lack AUROC/R² (only partial-r); among the Taiwanese EAS-only set, PGS003420 has the highest reported full-model AUROC.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely aligned aortic valve function measures mapped to aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92) in a large European evaluation (n=446,895). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, lipids, BMI, smoking, renal failure), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates. Runners-up: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis score with PRS-CS and a moderate-strong HR (1.64, with CI) but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS005255 and PGS005256 are aortic stenosis–mapped valve-function traits with similar design and HR (~1.53) but are less direct phenotype matches than explicit aortic stenosis; remaining candidates are non-matching (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), so they have substantially weaker direct-match support. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including two models explicitly mapped to EFO:arthritis (PGS001135 “Arthritis (nos)” and the “M13 (Other arthritis)” models PGS004477/PGS004547). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match because it is an explicit arthritis (EFO:arthritis) model with reported PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.53928; PGS R2 no covariates=0.00291) and incremental AUROC (0.00314), enabling interpretation of PRS contribution rather than relying only on full-model discrimination. The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to underperform disease-focused scores; additionally, its PRS-only signal is modest. Runners-up are other direct EFO:arthritis models: PGS004547 and PGS004477 (both “M13 (Other arthritis)”) but they report only an OR without PRS-only AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, making them less comparable; osteoarthritis umbrella direct matches (PGS001290, PGS001882) are included next as arthritis-spectrum direct matches but are not exact EFO:arthritis endpoints.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly a disease-focused pediatric asthma PRS (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) with strong PRS signal reported as an OR per SD of 1.57 (95% CI 1.55–1.60) and large-scale validation (n=391,820), while avoiding explicitly heavy clinical covariate packaging (covariates listed as Unknown rather than family-history/environmental bundles). The main limitation is endpoint specificity (pediatric asthma rather than generic asthma) and the lack of PRS-only AUROC/R2 metrics, so the choice is not unequivocally best for generic asthma risk.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; asthma; multi-biobank training cohorts; AUROC 0.659 and Nagelkerke R2 0.048844 with covariates regressed out) provides relatively PRS-comparable R2 evidence but appears to come from a global biobank framework context. PGS001787 is similar but with weaker reported R2 (0.035168). PGS001344 (snpnet; doctor-diagnosed asthma) has strong endpoint fidelity and the best full-model AUROC among the snpnet siblings shown (0.66621), but it is from a pan-trait UKB framework paper and its AUROC is full-model rather than explicitly PRS-only. PGS002061 (LDpred2; UKB portability study) has supportive partial correlation (0.1184) but lacks clearer PRS-only discrimination metrics and is also a framework/portability context, limiting confidence.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo includes atopic eczema). Ranking is driven primarily by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) and then by PRS-comparable performance evidence, per provided domain guidance.

Best: PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match because its endpoint is generic and deployment-aligned ("Incident atopic dermatitis"), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), and it reports a PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910). Limitations: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is reported, and the HR is modest.

Runners-up: (1) PGS004587 also targets "Incident atopic dermatitis" with an HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282) but is a sparse GWAS-significant SNP set (23 variants) with weaker effect size evidence. (2) PGS001773 has a more restricted endpoint ("Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis") and reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates; per guidance, full-model metrics are not a substitute for PRS-only metrics and the very high values are not directly comparable/sanity-checkable against eczema heritability. (3–4) PGS003486 and PGS003459 are further penalized because their phenotyping is therapy/context-specific ("Paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis"), making them less faithful to generic atopic eczema risk despite reporting ORs and AUROCs in that restricted setting.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top candidates lack PRS-only discrimination metrics and several alternatives have endpoint restrictions (severity-specific or paradoxical/treatment-induced phenotypes), leaving residual uncertainty despite clear direct-match presence.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial fibrillation) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally coherent phenotyping_reported. PGS005168 is best supported in the visible evidence because it comes from a disease-focused AF meta-analysis (Nat Genet; >180,000 cases per title), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), reports strong discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) and a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663), and uses mostly basic covariates plus CHARGE-AF (a clinical risk calculator) which is a comparability concern but does not negate the otherwise strong disease-focused evidence package. Runners-up: PGS002814 has very large multi-cohort GWAS support and strong OR (~1.94) with AUROC 0.74 but is East-Asian-evaluated (less directly comparable if deployment ancestry is unspecified). PGS005313 reports strong OR (1.82) and AUROC 0.78 with basic covariates, but is evaluated in a MAE-only context and has only one performance record shown. PGS000016 (LDpred, genome-wide) has explicit PRS-only R2 (0.029) consistent with the provided EUR heritability ceiling and large validation (n=288,978), but its reported AUROC is full-model and thus less PRS-comparable. PGS000331 is another disease-focused LDpred genome-wide score with HR 1.62 and C-index 0.751, but with smaller training/validation than the strongest meta-analysis-based options. Confidence is Moderate because several candidates report only full-model metrics, some have horizon/packaging or ancestry-evaluation constraints, and PGS005168 includes CHARGE-AF covariate adjustment which can inflate full-model discrimination relative to standalone PRS. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct-match in the sense that their trait_efo includes atrial flutter; however, only PGS001263 is specifically aligned to atrial flutter across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (all explicitly “Atrial flutter”), whereas the other three are broader “atrial fibrillation and flutter” composites (one is time-to-event). PGS001263 also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R²=0.025), enabling a heritability sanity check (PGS-only R² remains below the provided h2_obs=0.0157 / h2_liability=0.1443 ceiling guidance) and avoiding reliance on full-model AUROC. Main limitation: PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse snpnet framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; meanwhile the portability-study models (PGS002050, PGS001841) use stronger genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression methods and larger training n, but lack PRS-only AUROC/R² (only partial-r), and their endpoint is the broader AF+flutter composite, making the overall direct-match evidence set conflicted rather than clearly high-quality.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly autism spectrum disorder), it comes from an ASD-focused publication, and it reports stronger available performance evidence (full_model_r2=0.0245 plus OR=1.33 per SD) in a European validation context. PGS002790 is a weaker direct-match runner-up because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly not ASD ("Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)"), its reported metric is a smaller partial R² (~0.00546) with no effect sizes shown, and the publication framing is broader/cross-trait rather than ASD-focused—creating endpoint-fidelity and comparability concerns despite the trait_reported label. Confidence is Moderate because neither model provides clearly PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) AUC/R², and the selected R² values are full-model/partial metrics rather than unambiguously PRS-only.

All 20 listed candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates only (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest combined performance/effect-size evidence among the MGI-evaluated cluster: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), high Nagelkerke R² 0.0487, and strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR 3.61. Close runners-up are near-clone MGI models with essentially identical endpoint/covariates and very similar metrics: PGS000454 (AUROC 0.632; R² 0.0489; OR 1.661; top-1% OR 3.79), PGS000456 (AUROC 0.63; R² 0.0456; OR 1.633; top-1% OR 3.95), and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628; R² 0.0457; OR 1.634; top-1% OR 4.03). As the 4th runner-up, PGS000457 is preferred over other remaining options because it retains direct BCC endpoint fidelity and shows solid effect size (OR 1.535) with UKB development/validation, though its AUROC/R² are lower than the top MGI models. Confidence is Moderate because the top MGI candidates are extremely close and all reported AUROCs are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting comparability and making tie-breaking rely on small metric differences that may be noise. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (all map to bilirubin metabolism disease). PGS001824 is preferred because its phenotype is the most endpoint-faithful to the target (trait_efo exactly bilirubin metabolism disease; phenotyping_reported and trait_reported are specifically “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), and it reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0716 in European validation). PGS002032 is a near-clone with the same endpoint and identical partial-r, but differs mainly by method/structure (LDpred2 with 19,768 variants vs penalized regression with 22 variants); with no AUC/R² or other discriminative metrics provided for either, the evidence is insufficient to clearly favor one sibling over the other, lowering confidence. PGS000924 is a broader composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism” time-to-event) from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper; despite high reported AUROC/full-model metrics, domain guidance cautions that such framework sparse scores often generalize poorly and time-to-event/composite endpoints reduce endpoint fidelity versus the direct bilirubin-excretion diagnosis, so it ranks behind the two exact-endpoint siblings. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three visible candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to the target bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and similar basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), so there is no strong differentiator from study design or transportability. The main limitation is endpoint fidelity: each model’s phenotyping_reported is not a bipolar diagnosis endpoint (they reference cognitive/behavioral measures), making the direct-match evidence weaker despite the trait labels. With no PRS-comparable AUC/PRS-only R2 and only very small full_model_r2 values reported, performance evidence is also weak and not clearly comparable. Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is the closest concept match (not subtype-restricted) and has the largest variant count among the three, but this is only marginal support; runners-up are the subtype-specific siblings, with PGS002787 ranked ahead of PGS002788 due to slightly higher full_model_r2 (a weak tie-break).

All 3 visible candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target umbrella (“blood coagulation disease”), but they are all from pan-trait / portability-style UK Biobank framework papers rather than a disease-focused coagulation study family, which the provided domain guidance flags as a systematic weakness for external performance. Among the two models with the closest and most specific endpoint to coagulation disease (both are for “Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)” with identical phenotyping, cohorts, covariates, training size, and similar partial-r), PGS002034 is mildly preferred over PGS001826 on structural grounds (genome-wide shrinkage LDpred2 with many variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) while performance evidence is essentially indistinguishable (partial-r 0.0563 vs 0.0562). PGS001033 is a broader/less specific endpoint (“Other coagulation defects” time-to-event) and is from the ‘813 traits’ sparse framework with only 1 variant; despite having reported AUROC fields, its framework origin plus extreme sparsity and TTE endpoint reduce confidence that it is the best direct-match choice. Overall confidence is low because (i) the top two candidates are near-clones with only a weak differentiator, and (ii) none of the candidates provides strong, clearly PRS-comparable discrimination evidence (AUC/R2 are missing for the congenital-deficiency models, and the remaining AUC evidence is tied to a sparse pan-trait framework score).

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided list. The strongest-supported option is PGS004153 because it is a direct breast cancer model (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), evaluated in a large European validation set (n=48,968), uses a multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; a positive structural signal per domain guidance), and reports among the best discrimination/variance metrics within the visible set (full_model_auc=0.6625; full_model_r2=0.0764; OR per SD=1.83). Runners-up are selected from the same coherent, disease-endpoint-faithful 2023 Am J Hum Genet ‘five biobanks’ family (same phenotype, same validation size/ancestry, covariates=0), where differences are primarily in reported AUROC/R2/OR: PGS004040 and PGS004025 (LDpred2 variants) are very close to the best model on AUROC/R2/OR; PGS004083 and PGS004069 are next-best by the same metrics. Main limitation: the evidence shown is largely full-model metrics (and covariates are listed as 0, but PGS-only AUROC/R2 are not explicitly provided), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and confidence is reduced despite the strong, internally consistent cluster.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo and largely aligned phenotyping_reported. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets the exact disease endpoint (“Coeliac disease”), is from a disease-focused clinical-care/diagnosis-oriented study (not a pan-trait or portability framework), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), providing comparatively rich and stable-looking evidence within this candidate set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as “Unknown,” so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata, lowering certainty.

Runners-up: PGS001301 has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.82867; PGS R2 0.14224) and clear covariates, but comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable than disease-focused models when a disease-focused alternative exists. PGS000040 reports very high AUROC (0.9) in a disease-focused celiac study, but only as full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and smaller validation (n=2,476), making comparability uncertain. PGS000042 and PGS000041 are phenotype-restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint narrower than generic celiac disease) and have only full-model AUROC (~0.73), so they are weaker direct matches for the general target despite being disease-focused.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is preferred because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis study context (Hum Mol Genet 2023) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555), which is a positive structural signal for polygenic traits when endpoint alignment is acceptable. It also reports an HR per SD of 1.33 (moderate effect-size evidence) with basic covariates (age, smoking) and EUR evaluation.

Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-comparable metrics are sparse/inconsistent—most reported AUROC/C-index values appear to be full-model metrics (often with covariates), and only PGS001299 reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 but is from a pan-trait UKB framework (813 traits) with weak PGS-only discrimination (AUROC ~0.55; R2 ~0.0026), which domain guidance cautions against over-weighting. Because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only performance in a disease-focused setting, the choice relies heavily on endpoint fidelity + study archetype + method/structure, keeping confidence at Moderate.

Runner-up ordering: PGS000073 and PGS000784 are coherent incident cervical cancer models with similar covariates and moderate HR (~1.21–1.22) in large EUR evaluation (n~211,795), but they are sparse GWAS-hit style (10 variants) and their reported AUROC/C-index are full-model; PGS005165 is a direct-match EAS-focused model (useful for East Asian contexts) but has lower reported C-index (0.566) and is ancestry-specific; PGS003389 is disease-matched but shows weaker reported discrimination (AUROC 0.563; very low R2 0.00158) despite larger variant count than the GWAS-hit scores.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis via trait_efo/trait_reported, with two main endpoint families: (i) ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis (PGS004476, PGS004546) and (ii) combined cholelithiasis+cholecystitis (PGS001861, PGS002072), plus a time-to-event cholelithiasis framework score (PGS001174) and an East-Asian-evaluated cholelithiasis score (PGS005150). PGS004546 is preferred because it is tightly phenotype-aligned (K80 cholelithiasis) and provides the strongest available per-SD effect size evidence among the K80 siblings (OR 1.2986 vs 1.2194 for PGS004476), while avoiding the explicit pan-trait/framework penalty that applies to PGS001174 and the endpoint-broadening penalty of the cholecystitis-composite scores. However, overall evidence remains limited because the K80 models lack PRS-comparable AUC/R² and have unknown covariates, and several alternatives are plausible depending on desired ancestry/endpoint framing (e.g., PGS001174 has explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework; PGS002072/PGS001861 report partial-r but use a composite endpoint; PGS005150 is EAS-only evaluation and thus less generally supported in this context).

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (CKD) via trait_efo=chronic kidney disease, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable the reported performance is as PRS signal. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ (eGFR<45) and comes from a disease-focused CKD prediction study (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”, Nat Med) with multi-ancestry evaluation and a strong reported effect size (OR=1.47) plus a reported AUROC (0.78) in European validation. Although its AUROC is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (so not directly comparable as PRS-only), the combination of endpoint specificity, disease-focused study archetype, and effect-size support makes it the most defensible primary choice from the visible evidence.

Runners-up: PGS005090 has very strong reported full-model AUROC/R2 (0.9/0.1) and a solid OR (1.41) with an explicitly CKD stage 3+ framing in African-ancestry evaluation, but it is ancestry-specific (AFR-only GWAS/EVAL) and the very high full-model AUROC may be covariate-influenced, limiting general direct-match preference without a specified deployment ancestry. PGS004889 targets incident CKD (without diabetes) with multi-ancestry evaluation and HR=1.3, but it is incident/restricted (non-diabetic) and uses a bundled clinical risk score covariate package, making its discrimination less PRS-comparable. PGS005113 is CKD-labeled with OR=1.35 and CKDGen training, but lacks explicit PRS-comparable metrics and is embedded in a proteomic-marker context, leaving less direct evidence than the above. PGS002757 is a clean CKD label with modest OR=1.15 and limited performance detail, so it ranks behind stronger effect-size / study-design-supported options.

Main limitation lowering confidence: across the pool, PRS-only (no-covariate) discrimination metrics are largely absent, and several candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index with varying (sometimes heavy) covariate sets, making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain even among direct matches.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). PGS001783 is best supported overall because it is a direct COPD endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092), which is consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling guidance (h2_liability ~0.0388) and therefore passes the sanity-check. Main limitation: the publication context is a global biobank framework-style study and the reported AUROC (0.74) appears as a generic classification metric without an explicit PGS-only AUROC, so comparability across candidates is imperfect and confidence is not high.

Runners-up: PGS001788 is the closest competitor (same study family, same endpoint, PRS-CS-auto, similar variant count, much larger validation n but weaker PRS-comparable R2=0.0163). Among the UKB snpnet direct COPD siblings, PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334 are endpoint-faithful but come from a pan-trait sparse framework ("across 813 traits"), with low PGS-only AUROC (~0.54–0.55) and very small PGS-only R2 (~0.002–0.003), making them weaker than the PRS-CS-auto options; within that cluster, PGS001334 is slightly stronger on PGS-only metrics but is time-to-event labeled, while PGS001332 is the clean generic COPD label. Non-COPD emphysema (PGS001326) and chronic airway obstruction portability scores (PGS001850/PGS002062) are less directly aligned to the target label despite mapping to the COPD EFO, so they are not ranked ahead of the direct COPD-labeled models.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (cirrhosis of liver), with three being generic cirrhosis (PGS004621/PGS000726/PGS004621) and three being alcohol-related cirrhosis subtypes (PGS000704/PGS001777/PGS004913). PGS004621 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both ‘Cirrhosis’), a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and large multi-cohort disease-focused development/validation context (multiple biobanks listed; validation_sample_size n=1,153,995) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, confidence is limited because the only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (~0.68) rather than an explicit PRS-only metric, making cross-model performance comparability imperfect per the provided domain guidance.

The runners-up are subtype-specific JIA scores (oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular, enthesitis-related): they are direct matches only to sub-phenotypes rather than the broad target, so they are ranked behind the umbrella model despite some having higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000324 AUROC 0.93). Among subtypes, PGS000325 is ranked highest due to strong endpoint clarity and supportive AUROC/OR with large validation n, followed by PGS000326; PGS000324 is placed last because its very high full-model AUROC is not PRS-only and its endpoint is the narrowest subtype relative to the broad target. Overall confidence is moderate because the key performance evidence across all models is primarily full-model AUROC (not PRS-only), limiting comparability and strength of recommendation.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (kidney cancer) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (kidney cancer / renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; several explicitly use incident kidney cancer or malignant neoplasm of kidney). PGS004908 is best supported because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), reports the strongest visible PRS effect size (OR=1.5 per SD, 95% CI 1.43–1.58) and the highest reported discrimination among the pool (AUROC=0.74, albeit presented as a full-model metric), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical leakage. Main limitation: across candidates, PRS-only (covariate-free) AUC/R2 is not provided, so comparisons rely on effect sizes and full-model AUROC/C-index which are not strictly PRS-comparable; this keeps confidence at Moderate. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are coherent renal cell carcinoma / incident kidney cancer models with similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) and HR (~1.15–1.16) in large European evaluations; PGS000722 has weaker AUROC (0.567) but strong endpoint alignment and large evaluation; PGS004690 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (AnnoPred) with very large variant count but shows only modest AUROC (0.5644) and has unknown covariates, limiting interpretability.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS004562 and PGS004492 (trait_efo: kidney failure; phenotyping_reported: N18 chronic renal failure) and PGS000708 (trait_reported: Kidney failure but phenotyping_reported indicates diabetic kidney failure). PGS004562 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (explicit chronic renal failure/kidney failure code), genome-wide method/coverage (RFDiseasemetaPRS; ~1.06M variants), and stronger reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.395) than the other kidney-failure-coded sibling PGS004492 (OR=1.171). However, the overall evidence remains limited because these kidney-failure-coded models provide no PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²; covariates listed as Unknown), so the selection relies mainly on endpoint alignment plus effect size and structural signals. Runners-up: PGS002237 is a strong near-direct match (CKD stage 3+; disease-focused Nat Med; multi-ancestry evaluation; AUROC 0.78) but is not kidney-failure-specific; PGS000708 is kidney-failure-labeled but restricted to diabetic kidney failure and reports only full-model C-index; PGS004492 matches kidney failure but has weaker effect size than PGS004562; PGS001272 is a chronic renal failure TTE framework score with low PGS-only AUROC/R², making it a weaker direct-match despite having PRS-only metrics.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo maps to osteoarthritis, knee; trait/phenotyping are knee OA/gonarthrosis or closely related endpoints). PGS002767 is best supported because it has a directly aligned endpoint (“Knee osteoarthritis”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.3–1.4), which is a PRS-comparable signal when AUC/R2 are missing. The main limitation is that it lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and provides only a single performance record, so superiority over other genome-wide models cannot be confirmed from comparable discrimination metrics.

Runners-up: PGS002729 is also directly aligned and comes from a disease-focused OA PRS paper with reported AUROC=0.66, but this appears to be a full-model AUROC with covariates (age/sex/BMI) and no PRS-only metrics, limiting comparability. PGS004549 and PGS004479 are endpoint-aligned gonarthrosis scores with genome-wide variant counts and moderate ORs, but have unknown covariates and no AUC/R2, lowering confidence. PGS001192 is endpoint-aligned but comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (“across 813 traits”) and shows weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.56; PGS R2 0.0068), making it less supported despite richer metric reporting.

All 5 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, so a direct-match exists. PGS000054 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused LOAD PRS publication with a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) and basic covariates (age, sex), providing comparatively strong PRS-discrimination evidence among the pool; it also adds non-EUR evaluation (AMR/Hispanic or Latin American), which is supportive for broader transportability relative to EUR-only evaluations. Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R²; reported full-model metrics are either missing or not PRS-comparable, so ranking relies heavily on endpoint alignment plus effect sizes/structural metadata, lowering certainty.

Runners-up: PGS000053 is the closest sibling (same study, same 21 variants, same covariates) but with a weaker OR (1.29). PGS000334 reports an R²=0.191, but it is not explicitly PRS-only and is unusually high for C+T with unknown covariates, making it potentially non-comparable/suspect per the provided domain guidance. PGS004918 reports full-model AUROC=0.731 but with unknown covariates and very small development/validation (n=439 training; n=136 validation), so the AUROC is discounted and evidence is limited. PGS002289 has very large validation (n=497,087) but its phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than a direct LOAD diagnosis endpoint, reducing endpoint fidelity for a disease-risk PRS despite the trait label.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or closely synonymous endpoints like C34 malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung). PGS004860 is best supported in the visible list because it has a directly aligned endpoint (incident lung cancer), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2; ~1.14M variants), and reports strong discrimination in its selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.893 with tight CI) plus an effect size (OR 1.33). Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates (age/sex/BMI/smoking/PCs), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated; this prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ call. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000078 and its derivative PGS000789 have very large European validation (n=392,539) and consistent full-model AUROC (~0.846) with HR ~1.16–1.17 but include extensive smoking/environment/family-history covariates (more covariate-driven risk packaging). PGS000740 has strong reported full-model AUROC (0.811) and substantial development/validation support but is endpoint-restricted (early-onset <50) and framed as absolute-risk trajectory packaging. PGS000721 is a direct lung cancer endpoint with moderate full-model AUROC (0.738) and similar covariate set to several other smaller-AUC models, but offers less overall support than the higher-performing/stronger-evidence candidates above.

All 12 visible candidates are direct matches to the target concept (lupus erythematosus) via either the exact EFO term (PGS001870, PGS002082) or the closely aligned systemic lupus erythematosus endpoint (all others). The best-supported choice is PGS002082 because it has strong phenotype alignment ("Lupus (localized and systemic)"; trait_efo=lupus erythematosus; phenotyping_reported matches) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (361,553), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits over sparse/hits-only approaches when PRS-only metrics are otherwise limited. However, confidence is not high because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2; the available metrics are mostly full-model AUROC or partial correlation, and one high-AUROC candidate (PGS003960) is penalized by explicit phenotype-risk-score covariate packaging (comparability leakage), making cross-candidate performance comparisons uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS001870 is the same exact lupus erythematosus endpoint but is a much sparser penalized regression score (87 variants) with slightly weaker partial-r than PGS002082. Among disease-focused SLE scores, PGS000328 has relatively strong reported full-model AUROC (0.83) but is restricted to early-onset SLE and uses only genomewide-significant variants; PGS000754 is a genome-wide lassosum score with very large variant count but lower reported full-model AUROC (0.65) and mixed evaluation ancestries; PGS004917 is a direct SLE endpoint with supportive effect size (OR 2.01 reported) but includes smoking interaction framing and only full-model AUROC, limiting comparability.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait (lymphoid leukemia), including PGS000077, PGS000788, PGS000645, and PGS002305 (all mapped to trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia). PGS000077 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a coherent disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context; it also reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.45) supporting PRS signal. Among remaining direct matches, PGS000645 and PGS002305 have weaker reported AUROC (~0.58 and 0.57) and/or smaller validation (PGS002305 n=265), so they rank below. Non-exact EFO candidates for chronic lymphocytic leukemia are not prioritized here because the task is direct-match to lymphoid leukemia. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and in how PRS-comparable the reported metrics are.

Best pick: PGS004606 is the most supported direct-match overall because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics paper (Nat Genet 2024), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and reports a full-model AUROC (0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). It also reports an OR per SD of 1.76, which is strong supportive evidence of PRS discriminative signal.

Main limitation lowering confidence: across the candidate set, PRS-only (no-covariate) AUROC/R² is largely missing for the newer disease-focused models, so comparisons rely on a mix of full-model AUROC and effect sizes that are not perfectly comparable across studies.

Runner-up ordering logic (remaining direct-match support):
- PGS004952: very endpoint-faithful for late AMD and reports a very high AUROC, but the AUROC appears inconsistently encoded (classification_metrics shows 84.2 rather than 0.842) and validation n is small (n=1,232), making the performance evidence less reliable/comparable.
- PGS004607: same disease-focused Nat Genet 2024 family and method as PGS004606, but weaker reported AUROC (0.65) and OR (1.48).
- PGS001013: exact macular degeneration label and includes explicit PGS-only AUROC/R², but it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores; its PGS-only AUROC is modest (0.553).
- PGS002269: trait_reported is AMD, but phenotyping_reported is a retinal layer thickness biomarker endpoint rather than direct AMD diagnosis, making endpoint fidelity weaker for generic macular degeneration risk despite being disease-relevant.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). PGS002247 is best supported in the visible list because it has a tightly aligned endpoint (incident invasive melanoma), reports comparatively strong discrimination among melanoma-specific models with AUROC available (full_model_auc=0.691; R²=0.072), and comes from a melanoma-focused independent evaluation study (Br J Dermatol 2022) rather than a broad pan-trait framework. Key limitation: most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PGS-only AUROC/R²), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and the apparent AUROC advantage could partly reflect covariate context; additionally, several near-tied direct melanoma models exist (e.g., PGS002246 AUROC=0.688; PGS003382 AUROC=0.682; PGS000766 C-index=0.643), keeping confidence at Moderate.

All 6 candidates are nominal direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma), but one (PGS003450) has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported ("Chronic lymphocytic leukemia"), making it weaker for direct-match despite sharing the myeloma label elsewhere. Among the remaining coherent myeloma-endpoint models, PGS002281 is best supported by (i) phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Multiple myeloma), (ii) comparatively strong reported discrimination in the visible record (full_model AUROC 0.644 with CI) and a strong risk gradient (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), and (iii) basic demographic covariates (age/sex/region) without obvious clinical leakage. Confidence is only Moderate because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only metrics (the AUROCs shown are full-model), covariates are unknown for PGS002306, and PGS002306 shows an even higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) with less transparent covariate comparability, leaving some unresolved competition. Runners-up are ranked by remaining endpoint fidelity plus the strength/clarity of the visible performance evidence and covariate transparency: PGS002306 next (higher AUROC but small n and unknown covariates), then the PRSweb cluster (PGS000653/PGS000654/PGS000652) with consistent myeloma phenotyping and basic covariates but lower full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and weaker effect-size evidence.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (IMSGC), endpoint-aligned (multiple sclerosis), EUR GWAS/EVAL matched, and has the strongest reported discrimination among candidates with AUROC evidence (full-model AUROC=0.80 with an additional strong effect-size-style metric: OR top 10% vs median=15.0). However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC is full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), covariates are listed as Unknown (limiting comparability), and several other direct-match models either lack PRS-only metrics (PGS000809/PGS004699) or come from framework/portability studies with weaker PRS-comparable signals (PGS001270/PGS001271/PGS001831/PGS002038). Runners-up are ranked by remaining support: PGS000809 (disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS context with reported full-model AUROC/R² and basic covariates), then the two UKB portability framework scores with slightly stronger partial-r (PGS002038 > PGS001831), then PGS004699 (endpoint-aligned but appears more like a prediction-at-presentation context and provides only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics).

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction, including PheCode 411.2 and ICD10 I21 acute MI). Among the visible direct-match set, PGS005039 is best supported because it is endpoint-aligned (Myocardial infarction; PheCode 411.2), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (ldpred) with very large variant count (1,286,612), and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the MI PheCode cluster (full-model C-index 0.7848) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so cross-model comparability is imperfect; additionally, several near-clone MI PheCode models from the same publication have extremely similar C-index/OR evidence, making the top choice not uniquely decisive. Runners-up are selected from the same MI PheCode family with similarly strong C-index (~0.783–0.784) and OR (~1.53–1.55): PGS005035, PGS005045, PGS005044, then PGS005038.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; trait_efo = Nasal Cavity Polyp; phenotyping_reported = J33) with identical ancestry context (DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), training cohort (UKB), training size (n=174,489), validation size (n=56,192), and identical variant count (1,059,939) from the same publication family. However, confidence is limited because covariates are listed as Unknown for both and key comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2) are missing, leaving only a single effect-size record to separate near-clones.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and report the same endpoint label/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder) from the same UKB portability publication with similar training (UKB; n=391,124), validation size (n=19,400), and basic covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs). With endpoint fidelity essentially tied, the main differentiator in visible evidence is PRS-comparable performance: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a supportive structural signal for polygenic traits. However, confidence is limited because both models come from a portability/framework-style UKB paper (a known weaker archetype vs disease-focused studies) and neither provides AUC/R2 or effect-size metrics in the visible record, leaving only partial-r for discrimination comparison.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter) via either explicit benign nodular goiter endpoints (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263) or closely aligned nontoxic multinodular goiter endpoints (PGS001814/PGS002022). The strongest direct-match support is for PGS005262 because it targets the most semantically aligned endpoint (“Benign nodular goiter”), comes from a disease-focused multi-biobank thyroid disease study family (many contributing cohorts listed), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count, and has the best reported discrimination among the benign nodular goiter models (full-model AUROC 0.5933) plus a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.41). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005273 and PGS005274 are still nodular-goiter–anchored but are case-control contrasts (“thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter”), so they are slightly less endpoint-faithful to generic nodular goiter despite higher AUROC/OR; PGS005263 is the closest sibling to the best model but with weaker AUROC/OR; PGS005261 is the same endpoint but uses a sparse P+T approach with far fewer variants and weaker effect size (OR 1.05). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because the key performance evidence for the 2026 models is primarily full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (limiting PRS-only comparability), and the alternative UKB portability scores (PGS001814/PGS002022) report only small partial correlations, making cross-study performance comparison uncertain.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. PGS005235 is best supported because its endpoint is explicitly obesity diagnosis anchored to a phecode ("Obesity (phecode: 278.1)"), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with substantial variant count (709,828), and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97), which domain guidance treats as strong discrimination evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Runners-up: PGS004447 (E66 obesity; LDpred2; very large variant count; moderate OR≈1.36 but covariates unknown), PGS005154 (obesity; CT-SLEB; EAS evaluation; effect size reported but not directly comparable to OR/HR), PGS005145 (obesity; PRS-CS; EAS-only GWAS/EVAL; effect size reported but not directly comparable), and PGS004517 (E66 obesity; metaPRS-style method; OR≈1.23). Confidence is not high because most candidates lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2), several have unknown covariates, and two strong-method candidates are EAS-only evaluations (transportability unclear if deployment ancestry is not EAS).

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo includes osteoporosis and phenotyping_reported is osteoporosis or an ICD10-aligned subtype such as M81). The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS001273 because it has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance reporting (explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.5685 with CI and PGS-only R2=0.00688) on a directly aligned osteoporosis endpoint with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). PGS001274 is a close runner-up with slightly stronger PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.57595; PGS-only R2=0.00945) but its endpoint is time-to-event ‘osteoporosis without pathological fracture’, which is a narrower/horizon-style formulation than generic osteoporosis and is flagged as a potential fidelity penalty in the provided domain guidance. Remaining runners-up are ranked by endpoint alignment plus available PRS-signal evidence: PGS002768 reports a moderate per-SD OR=1.31 (EUR eval) on osteoporosis (though it also mentions heel BMD in trait_efo and lacks AUC/R2), and among the 2024 Commun Biol cluster with unknown covariates and only ORs, PGS004565 (OR≈1.328) and PGS004560 (OR≈1.321) have the strongest visible effect sizes. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because much of the candidate set lacks PRS-comparable metrics (AUC/R2) and several come from framework/portability-style studies or have unknown covariates, leaving meaningful uncertainty despite direct phenotype matches.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to otosclerosis with trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is a straightforward disease endpoint (“Otosclerosis”), whereas PGS001255 uses a time-to-event endpoint (“TTE otosclerosis”), which domain guidance flags as a potential weakness for generic disease-risk deployment when not clearly outweighed by stronger study-family evidence. Direct-match candidates are present, including multiple models explicitly mapped to the target EFO term (ovarian neoplasm) with phenotyping_reported = "Malignant neoplasm of ovary" (PGS000544–PGS000564 family), as well as near-synonymous ovarian carcinoma/cancer models. All 11 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma endpoints, with one clinically dominant subtype model (PGS002264; pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also plausibly aligned. All 11 listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease throughout, except PGS000777 which is Parkinson’s disease dementia/progression). Direct-match candidates are present (4 total) spanning peripheral vascular disease (unspecified) and peripheral artery/arterial disease. PGS005217 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is a direct clinical endpoint (incident peripheral artery disease), it comes from a disease-focused PAD study (JAMA Cardiol) with broad multi-cohort development and large multi-ancestry evaluation, and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.66, 95% CI 1.61–1.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is comparatively clean and PRS-informative. Runners-up: Among the two UKB portability-framework ‘peripheral vascular disease, unspecified’ scores, PGS002055 (LDpred2; 599,514 variants) is preferred over PGS001843 (penalized regression; 242 variants) due to stronger genome-wide shrinkage structure and slightly higher partial-r (0.0175 vs 0.0151) in the selected European validation record, but both are penalized by being from a portability framework with weak PRS signal (small partial-r). PGS005158 is a direct PAD candidate but is least supported due to very small variant count (19), restricted phenotype context (PAD in type 2 diabetes), and heavy covariate set including treatments/clinical factors, with only a modest HR (1.13).

All three visible candidates are direct-match on concept via trait_efo=preeclampsia, but endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) is mixed: PGS003586 and PGS003587 both use a pre-eclampsia/eclampsia phenotype (strong alignment to target), whereas PGS004593 is labeled preeclampsia but reports phenotyping as gestational hypertension (endpoint mismatch signal per domain guidance). Between the two endpoint-faithful siblings from the same Nat Med disease-focused study family (both PRS-CS, similar variant counts, same EUR evaluation, same validation n=25,582, and similarly basic covariates), PGS003586 has the stronger reported per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20), which is supportive evidence for better PRS discrimination when AUC/R2 are missing for all models.
